topics: 🪦 Rabbi Shimon Purifies Tiberias — testing hard and soft ground for hidden graves
😔 The Elder's Mockery — a fatal rebuke about criticizing from within the group
🗣️ Three Things Before Shabbat — tithes, eiruv, and the lamp
🌗 Doubtful Dusk — what may and may not be done when nightfall is uncertain
📜 One Verse, Two Reasons — deriving the Friday-evening checklist from Job 5:24
⏳ How Long Is Twilight? — Rabbi Yehuda, Rabbi Nechemya, and Rabbi Yosei disagree

overview.title: 📖 Overview: From a Purified Marketplace to the Boundaries of Twilight
overview.subtitle: Shabbat 34a–34b
overview.hebrewSource: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים צָרִיךְ אָדָם לוֹמַר בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת עִם חֲשֵׁכָה
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The daf opens with the dramatic end of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai's purification of the Tiberias marketplace, a story of both careful halakhic method and a fatal rebuke. The mishna then turns to a wholly different concern: what a person must say at home just before Shabbat, and what happens when nightfall itself is in doubt. The Gemara traces the mishna's checklist to a verse in Job, explains why the mishna's own two halves seem to contradict each other, and finally maps out the disputed physical signs and durations of twilight (bein hashemashot) — the razor's edge between the last permitted acts of Friday and the first prohibitions of Shabbat.

slides.title: 🪦 Purifying the Marketplace of Tiberias
slides.subtitle: Ground hard or soft, and a rebuke that cost two lives
slides.hebrewSource: כָּאן קִיצֵּץ בֶּן זַכַּאי תּוּרְמְסֵי תְּרוּמָה
slides.label: The method and its cost:
slides.text: Priests were troubled by suspected corpse-impurity in the Tiberias marketplace. An Elder told Rabbi Shimon that Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai once grew teruma lupines there, proving parts were pure. Rabbi Shimon then examined the ground itself: wherever it was hard he declared it pure (no burial possible), wherever soft he marked it as doubtful. When that same Elder later mocked him publicly — 'Ben Yochai purified the cemetery!' — Rabbi Shimon answered that since the Elder had been counted among those who ruled on it, mocking it now would make Torah scholars look like feuding rivals, worse than prostitutes who still help each other look presentable. He fixed his gaze on the Elder, who died; then, seeing Yehuda ben Gerim, who had caused the whole affair, in the marketplace, he fixed his gaze on him too and turned him into a pile of bones.

slides.title: 🗣️ Three Things a Person Must Say Friday at Dusk
slides.subtitle: The mishna's checklist, and what changes when nightfall is only a doubt
rows: May not tithe definitely-untithed produce; may tithe demai (doubtfully-tithed)
One may still insulate hot water; may not immerse impure vessels or light the lamp

callout.label: Source verse:
callout.text: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi derives the obligation to ask from Job 5:24: 'וְיָדַעְתָּ כִּי שָׁלוֹם אָהֳלֶךָ וּפָקַדְתָּ נָוְךָ וְלֹא תֶחֱטָא' — 'you shall know your tent is at peace, and you shall visit your habitation, and not sin.'

slides.title: 🤔 Why Does the Mishna Seem to Contradict Itself?
slides.subtitle: It bars action at 'doubtful dusk' — yet permits placing an eiruv at exactly that time

lines.speaker: Gemara
lines.text: The mishna says these things must be said 'at dusk,' implying that during doubtful dusk one may not act. But then it teaches that one may place an eiruv during doubtful dusk!

lines.speaker: Rav
lines.text: No contradiction. The first clause speaks of עֵירוּבֵי תְּחוּמִין (Shabbat-boundary eiruvin), a Torah-level matter requiring certainty. The second speaks of עֵירוּבֵי חֲצֵרוֹת (courtyard eiruvin), a lighter rabbinic stringency.

lines.speaker: Rabba b. R. Huna
lines.text: Even so — these three things must be said calmly, so the household will actually accept them and not be provoked into ignoring the warning.

lines.speaker: Rav Ashi
lines.text: I never heard that teaching stated explicitly, but I arrived at the very same practice on my own, through plain reasoning.

callout.label: Takeaway:
callout.text: A Torah-level eiruv needs certainty before dusk; a rabbinic one tolerates the uncertainty of twilight itself.

slides.title: 🎲 Rava's Case: Two People, One Agent, One Twilight
slides.subtitle: Both acquire the eiruv — no matter which way twilight actually falls

nodes.content: ❓ An agent places an eiruv while it is still day for person A, and at twilight for person B
🍽️ Both eiruvin get 'eaten' — A's during twilight, B's after nightfall

columns.label: If twilight = day
columns.content: B's eiruv (placed at twilight) should count; A's should not, since it was consumed while still day

columns.label: If twilight = night
columns.content: A's eiruv should count; B's should not, since it was placed too late

nodes.content: ✅ Rava's ruling: twilight's status is unresolved doubt, and rabbinic-level doubt is decided leniently — both acquire their eiruv

callout.label: Principle:
callout.text: סְפֵקָא דְרַבָּנַן לְקוּלָּא — uncertainty in a rabbinic law is resolved leniently.

slides.title: ⏳ How Long Does Twilight Last?
slides.subtitle: Three tannaim, three different clocks for bein hashemashot

boxes.title: Rabbi Yehuda
items: From sunset while the eastern sky still reddens
Lower sky faded, upper still red = still twilight
Upper sky faded and matches lower = night

boxes.title: Rabbi Nechemya
items: The time it takes to walk half a mil after sunset
Test: watch the sun atop Mount Carmel, then descend and immerse in the sea

boxes.title: Rabbi Yosei
items: Twilight is like the blink of an eye
Night enters and day leaves in that instant
Its duration cannot really be measured at all

callout.label: Why it matters:
callout.text: The baraita imposes the stringencies of both days on this uncertain window — relevant, for example, to a zav who saw an emission during twilight, whose day-count for impurity and offerings becomes doubtful.

summary.principle: Because twilight's status as day or night is genuinely uncertain, rabbinic-level halakhot (like courtyard eiruvin) are decided leniently through it, while Torah-level halakhot (like boundary eiruvin) require certainty beforehand — and the Sages disagree sharply on how long that uncertain window actually lasts.

flowSteps.content: 🪦 Rabbi Shimon purifies the Tiberias marketplace by testing hard vs. soft ground
🗣️ Mishna: before Shabbat, ask about tithes, eiruv, and lighting the lamp — derived from Job 5:24
⚖️ Apparent contradiction resolved: boundary-eiruv needs certainty; courtyard-eiruv tolerates doubtful dusk

columns.content: 🎲 Rava: two eiruvin, one before dusk, one during — both acquired, since rabbinic doubt is lenient
⏳ Twilight's length itself is disputed: color-change (R' Yehuda), half a mil (R' Nechemya), a blink (R' Yosei)

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: uncertainty at twilight is resolved leniently for rabbinic law, but never for Torah law

quiz.q: What convinced Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai that parts of the Tiberias marketplace were definitely pure?
o: A prophetic dream
An Elder recalled that Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai once grew teruma lupines there
The ground was uniformly hard everywhere
A count of the city's graves
quiz.e: An Elder told him that ben Zakkai, a priest, had planted and harvested teruma lupines there — proof the spot was presumed pure.

quiz.q: According to the mishna, what are the three things a person must say at home on Friday at dusk?
o: Have you prayed? Have you eaten? Have you rested?
Have you tithed? Have you made an eiruv? Light the lamp
Have you bathed? Have you dressed? Light the candles
Have you locked the door? Fed the animals? Swept the house?
quiz.e: The mishna lists: ask whether tithes were separated, whether the eiruv was placed, and then instruct that the lamp be lit.

quiz.q: During 'doubtful dusk' (safek chashecha), which of the following is still permitted according to the mishna?
o: Lighting the Shabbat lamp
Immersing ritually impure vessels
Tithing produce known to be definitely untithed
Insulating hot water for Shabbat
quiz.e: The mishna permits tithing demai, placing an eiruv, and insulating hot water during doubtful dusk, but not lighting the lamp, immersing vessels, or tithing definitely-untithed produce.

quiz.q: How does Rav resolve the apparent contradiction between the mishna's opening (implying no action at doubtful dusk) and its later permission to place an eiruv then?
o: The mishna is simply mistaken
The opening refers to Torah-level boundary eiruvin, which need certainty; the later clause refers to rabbinic courtyard eiruvin
Both clauses refer to the same type of eiruv
The contradiction is never resolved
quiz.e: Rav distinguishes eiruvei techumin (Torah law, requiring certainty) from eiruvei chatzerot (rabbinic, tolerant of the doubt of twilight).

quiz.q: In Rava's case of two eiruvin placed for two different people — one before dusk, one during twilight — what is the ruling?
o: Neither one acquires a valid eiruv
Only the one placed before dusk is valid
Only the one placed during twilight is valid
Both acquire their eiruv, because uncertainty in rabbinic law is decided leniently
quiz.e: Since twilight's status as day or night is unresolved, and this is a rabbinic-level question, the doubt is resolved leniently for both people.
